Offense vs Defense

Updated October 14, 2026 · US sector risk-on / risk-off gauge

Risk-on since July 31, 2026: the ratio is 1.2% above its 200-day average.

This chart compares the market's offensive sectors with its defensive ones. Offensive sectors (technology, consumer discretionary, communication services, financials and industrials) do best when investors are confident and the economy is growing. Defensive sectors (consumer staples, utilities and health care) hold up better when investors are worried, because people keep buying groceries, paying utility bills and seeing doctors in any economy.

We track the offensive group's performance relative to the defensive group's. When offense is outperforming, investors are leaning into risk. When defense is outperforming, they are seeking safety. The bottom panel shows how far that relationship sits above or below its own 200-day average. Above zero signals a risk-on market, below zero a risk-off market, and the further from zero, the stronger the lean.

Risk-on (above zero)   Risk-off (below zero)
The S&P 500 line turns blue during risk-off periods.
Each group is an equal-weighted basket of the Select Sector SPDR ETFs (XLK, XLY, XLC, XLF, XLI versus XLP, XLU, XLV), including dividends. Daily closes since 1998; communication services (XLC) joins in 2018.
